title: prez slide counter drops below the 4.5:1 contrast floor on dark slides and no theme can reach it
body:
## Summary

`prez`'s slide counter is `position: fixed` and a **sibling** of `.gp-deck`, not a descendant of the current slide. No theme selector can reach it per-slide, so on a dark section slide it renders at **3.42:1** against its background, below the 4.5:1 floor AC09 sets for every built-in.

Reported by `_tools-cc` as a consumer, from hv presenting a real 14-slide client deck on 2026-08-29. Not found by any check: AT08 measures per-theme legibility and passed.

## Why the suite did not catch it

Two reasons, and both are worth keeping.

- The counter is `aria-hidden` decorative chrome, so a contrast probe scoped to *text* legitimately skips it. Whether the floor applies to decorative chrome is a real question, not an oversight.
- Even a probe that measured it could not attribute the failure to a theme, because **no theme can fix it**. It needs the compiler to inherit the current slide's colour or carry a blend mode.

## Severity

Low. It is decorative, `aria-hidden`, and legible on most slides. Filed rather than fixed inline because it shipped: hv presented with it today, and a defect that shipped earns an issue even when the fix lands inside a steel thread (hv, 2026-07-29 precedent).

## Where the fix belongs

ST0010/WP-05 (default theme polish). The fix is in the compiler, not in any theme.

## Status of the stated home, and what actually blocks this (vc, 2026-09-08)

**ST0010/WP-05 is CANCELLED, so the home named above no longer exists.** Recorded rather than re-homed: picking a new home somewhere convenient is the thing to avoid, and under hv's 2026-07-10 ruling a tracked issue can drive a focused bugfix without a thread at all -- so this record can be its own home if hv wants it that way.

**THE RE-HOMING IS NOT THE ONLY BLOCKER, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING BEFORE SOMEONE CLEARS IT AND EXPECTS THE FIX TO FOLLOW.** Two more, both hv's:

- **The floor's scope is an open question this issue raises and does not settle**: whether 4.5:1 applies to `aria-hidden` decorative chrome. Answering "yes" by implementing a fix would settle it silently, in code, which is how a policy gets made by accident.
- **The fix changes approved output.** Correcting the colour alone is not enough -- the counter has no `color` of its own and inherits, and it is `opacity: 0.45` that carries it under the floor. So any real fix raises the opacity or otherwise makes the chrome more present on all seven themes, which hv page-turned and approved on 2026-09-08.

**The colour half is mechanically straightforward and is not the hard part.** The compiler already marks each slide `.gp-on-dark` / `.gp-on-light` and redefines `--gp-fg` on it; the counter cannot be reached by those selectors only because it is `position: fixed` and a sibling of `.gp-deck`. The runtime already rewrites the counter on every slide change (`html.rs`, the `counter.textContent` line), so mirroring the current slide's state onto `body` would let the same tokens reach it. That much is a small, well-fenced change. It is the opacity, and the question above it, that need hv.
